Automated metadata extraction for the pilot-study assessment

Method, validation and coverage across the pilot-1 and pilot-2 samples

Published

August 19, 2026

Code 
# run_pipeline.R sources its modules by relative path, so chunks run from the
# project root rather than from docs/.
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)
library(here)
library(scales)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
            theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  plot.title.position = "plot"))

PAL <- c("#3B6EA5", "#C1666B", "#7FB069", "#E5A34B", "#8A7090", "#9AA5B1")

read_out <- function(f) read_csv(here(f), show_col_types = FALSE)

pilot_val <- read_out("data/final_extraction_pilot1-and-pilot2.csv")
idx1      <- read_out("data/full_sample_index.csv")
ex1       <- read_out("data/final_extraction_full-empirical-sample.csv")
idx2      <- read_out("data/pilot2_sample_index.csv")
ex2       <- read_out("data/final_extraction_pilot2-sample.csv")

# The 20 extraction columns are identical across the two frames, so the samples
# stack once each row is labelled with the frame it came from.
combined <- bind_rows(
  ex1 |> mutate(frame = "pilot-1 frame"),
  ex2 |> mutate(frame = "pilot-2 frame")
)

n_frame1 <- nrow(idx1 |> filter(article_status != "pilot2"))
n_frame2 <- nrow(idx2)
n_ex1    <- nrow(ex1)
n_ex2    <- nrow(ex2)

What this is

This meta-scientific assessment asks how psychology articles report pilot studies, and whether articles that report one differ from those that do not on transparency and governance markers — journal transparency policy, funding, conflicts of interest and preregistration. Answering that needs those markers for every article in the sampling frame, not only for the articles a human coded.

This report documents the automated pipeline that produces them: what each column means, how accurate it is against manual coding, and what the two samples now contain.

The unit of analysis is the article, identified by DOI. Every article contributes at most one row.

The two samples

The project drew two sampling frames, one for each pilot round. They are independent draws from different search strategies and overlap in a single article, so their extraction outputs stack into one dataset.

Code 
tibble(
  Frame = c("Pilot-1 frame", "Pilot-2 frame"),
  `Source file` = c("full_sample.csv", "pilot2_sample.csv"),
  `Articles in frame` = c(n_frame1, n_frame2),
  `Manually coded` = c(
    sum(idx1$article_status == "pilot1"),
    sum(idx2$article_status == "pilot2-coded")),
  `Extraction rows` = c(n_ex1, n_ex2)
) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Sampling frames and extraction coverage") |>
  fmt_integer(columns = where(is.numeric)) |>
  cols_align("left", columns = c(Frame, `Source file`))

The two frames are filtered differently, and this matters for any analysis that pools them:

  • Pilot-1 frame — extraction is restricted to articles an LLM classifier marked as empirical, plus every manually coded article regardless of that classification. Articles classified non-empirical are in the index but carry no extraction row.
  • Pilot-2 frame — extracted unfiltered. The classifier has run over the pilot-1 frame only, so no empirical column exists for pilot 2.

To pool the frames on comparable terms, filter the pilot-1 rows on empirical == "yes" in data/full_sample_index.csv and accept that the pilot-2 rows are unrestricted, or run the classifier over the pilot-2 abstracts first.

Coverage within each frame

Code 
cov1 <- idx1 |>
  filter(article_status != "pilot2") |>
  mutate(state = case_when(
    doi %in% ex1$doi                  ~ "extracted",
    is.na(tei_file)                   ~ "no TEI (PDF not converted)",
    TRUE                              ~ "excluded: not classified empirical")) |>
  count(state, name = "Pilot-1 frame")

cov2 <- idx2 |>
  mutate(state = case_when(
    doi %in% ex2$doi ~ "extracted",
    is.na(tei_file)  ~ "no TEI (PDF not converted)",
    TRUE             ~ "TEI present but no extraction row")) |>
  count(state, name = "Pilot-2 frame")

full_join(cov1, cov2, by = "state") |>
  arrange(desc(coalesce(`Pilot-1 frame`, 0L) + coalesce(`Pilot-2 frame`, 0L))) |>
  rename(Status = state) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Article status within each sampling frame") |>
  fmt_integer(columns = where(is.numeric)) |>
  sub_missing(missing_text = "—")

Method

Inputs

Each article enters the pipeline as a DOI plus a path to a GROBID TEI file — a structured XML rendering of the article PDF, with headings, sections and back-matter marked up. TEI gives the extractors document structure, so a funding statement can be located by its heading rather than by scanning prose.

PDF → TEI conversion runs as a GitHub Action in the companion pilot2_pdf_conversion repository: the PDFs live in a Google Drive folder, a fleet of parallel runners each convert a share of them through GROBID 0.8.2.1-full, and one job commits the result.

DOI → TEI matching is deterministic. TEI filenames carry the DOI with every / flattened to -, and a DOI suffix can itself contain -, so the slashes cannot be restored by position. Both sides are therefore compared on a key that lower-cases the DOI and rewrites / as -.

The four extraction modules

Code 
tibble(
  Module = c("1. DOI metadata", "2. TEI funding & COI",
             "3. Preregistration", "4. Funder → country"),
  Source = c("OpenAlex + Crossref APIs", "GROBID TEI",
             "GROBID TEI + OSF API", "Crossref Funder Registry + OpenAlex/ROR"),
  Produces = c(
    "Journal, ISSN, SJR, TOP Factor, first-author affiliation, structured funder IDs, Crossref COI text, abstract",
    "Funding statement and conflict-of-interest statement text, located by document structure",
    "Preregistration present, platform, URL; registered-report and trial-registry flags",
    "Country for every named or ID-matched funder")
) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Pipeline modules") |>
  cols_width(Produces ~ px(420)) |>
  cols_align("left", columns = everything())

Two design choices are worth stating explicitly.

Preregistration is gated on the registration template, not on the word. An OSF link alone does not count: the pipeline resolves the OSF GUID through the OSF API and asks whether the object is a registration and, if so, under which template. An OSF project link is recorded as such and does not set prereg_present. Trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov and equivalents) and AsPredicted are detected separately, and registration_any is the union of preregistration, registered report and trial registry.

Conflict of interest is classified by negation, not by presence. A COI statement is first located (TEI, falling back to the Crossref deposit); a case-insensitive negation regex then decides whether it declares no conflict. No statement at all is a third, distinct category — the absence of a declaration is a finding, not a missing value.

Caching

Every networked lookup — OpenAlex and Crossref metadata, OSF GUIDs and registration templates, funder ID and funder name resolution — is cached to disk. A rerun over the same DOIs makes no network calls, and run_pipeline(..., use_api = FALSE) errors rather than silently reaching the network, which is what makes the outputs reproducible offline.

The 20 output columns

Code 
tibble::tribble(
  ~Column, ~Meaning,
  "doi", "Article DOI, normalised to lower case (join key)",
  "journal, issn", "Venue name and primary ISSN",
  "top_factor, sjr", "Journal transparency (TOP Factor) and Scimago (SJR) scores",
  "first_author_country", "First author's country, preferring the article-level affiliation over the author's OpenAlex profile",
  "first_author_location_full", "Institution, city, region, country for the same",
  "first_author_location_source", "Which of the two supplied the location",
  "funding_category", "funded / no funding / no statement",
  "funding_statement", "The extracted funding text (audit trail)",
  "funders", "Named funders, ||-separated",
  "funding_country", "Distinct funder countries, ||-separated",
  "coi_statement", "The extracted conflict-of-interest text (audit trail)",
  "coi_category", "conflict declared / no conflict declared / no statement",
  "prereg_present", "Whether the article reports a study preregistration",
  "prereg_platform", "OSF registration, AsPredicted, ClinicalTrials.gov, …",
  "prereg_url", "Registration link(s)",
  "is_registered_report", "Registered Report",
  "is_trial_registry", "Trial or health-registry entry",
  "registration_any", "Any of the three above"
) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Output schema") |>
  cols_width(Column ~ px(220), Meaning ~ px(480)) |>
  cols_align("left", columns = everything())

Validation against manual coding

Two rounds of manual coding provide the ground truth: 162 articles in pilot 1 and 184 in pilot 2. Three pipeline outputs have a manual counterpart in the coding form — funding_category, coi_category and prereg_present. Agreement is measured only on articles where a coder gave an answer.

Code 
source(here("run_pipeline.R"))

m1 <- read.csv(here("data/inputs/2025-12-09_Codingform_PilotingAssessment_pilot.csv"),
               check.names = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
m2 <- read.csv(here("data/inputs/2026-04-03_Codingform_PilotingAssessment_pilot2.csv"),
               check.names = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

man <- bind_rows(
  tibble(doi = norm_doi(m1[["X1.2..Article.DOI"]]), pilot = "pilot 1",
         mfund   = m1[["X8.1..Does.the.article.include.a.funding.statement."]],
         mcoi    = m1[["X8.2..Does.the.article.include.a.statement.indicating.whether.there.were.any.conflicts.of.interest."]],
         mprereg = m1[["X2.2...Does.the.article.state.whether.or.not.reported.study.studies.were.preregistered."]]),
  tibble(doi = norm_doi(m2[["X1.2..Article.DOI"]]), pilot = "pilot 2",
         mfund   = m2[["X8.1..Does.the.article.include.a.funding.statement."]],
         mcoi    = m2[["X8.2..Does.the.article.include.a.statement.indicating.whether.there.were.any.conflicts.of.interest..COI.."]],
         mprereg = m2[["X2.2...According.to.what.is.stated.in.the.article..were.the.reported.study.ies..preregistered.."]])
) |>
  filter(doi != "", doi != "test") |>
  distinct(doi, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    man_fund   = mapply(manual_funding_category, mfund, ifelse(pilot == "pilot 1", "pilot1", "pilot2")),
    man_coi    = vapply(mcoi, manual_coi_category, character(1)),
    man_prereg = vapply(mprereg, manual_prereg, logical(1)))

val <- pilot_val |> inner_join(man, by = "doi")

acc <- function(d, auto, manual) {
  keep <- !is.na(d[[manual]]) & !is.na(d[[auto]])
  tibble(n = sum(keep), agree = sum(d[[auto]][keep] == d[[manual]][keep])) |>
    mutate(accuracy = agree / n)
}

metrics <- bind_rows(
  lapply(c("pilot 1", "pilot 2"), function(p) {
    d <- val |> filter(pilot == p)
    bind_rows(
      acc(d, "funding_category", "man_fund")   |> mutate(Field = "funding_category"),
      acc(d, "coi_category",     "man_coi")    |> mutate(Field = "coi_category"),
      acc(d, "prereg_present",   "man_prereg") |> mutate(Field = "prereg_present")
    ) |> mutate(Round = p)
  }),
  {
    d <- val
    bind_rows(
      acc(d, "funding_category", "man_fund")   |> mutate(Field = "funding_category"),
      acc(d, "coi_category",     "man_coi")    |> mutate(Field = "coi_category"),
      acc(d, "prereg_present",   "man_prereg") |> mutate(Field = "prereg_present")
    ) |> mutate(Round = "pooled")
  })
Code 
metrics |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%.3f (%d/%d)", accuracy, agree, n)) |>
  select(Field, Round, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Round, values_from = cell) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "Accuracy against manual coding") |>
  cols_align("left", columns = Field)

What a blank funding field means

The pilot-1 coding form asked for the funding statement as free text. Coders filled it in when funding existed and left it empty otherwise, so a blank cannot separate the article has no funding statement from the coder did not transcribe one. Blanks are therefore treated as uncoded and excluded from the funding comparison.

Code 
mc <- read_out("data/cache/pipeline_metadata_cache.csv") |>
  mutate(doi = norm_doi(doi)) |>
  select(doi, funding_funder_ids_crossref)

blank1 <- val |>
  filter(pilot == "pilot 1", is.na(mfund) | trimws(mfund) == "") |>
  left_join(mc, by = "doi")

n_blank      <- nrow(blank1)
n_blank_fund <- sum(blank1$funding_category == "funded", na.rm = TRUE)
bf <- blank1 |> filter(funding_category == "funded")
n_blank_tei  <- sum(!is.na(bf$funding_statement) & nzchar(bf$funding_statement))
n_blank_xref <- sum(!is.na(bf$funding_funder_ids_crossref) &
                      nzchar(bf$funding_funder_ids_crossref))
n_blank_none <- sum((is.na(bf$funding_statement) | !nzchar(bf$funding_statement)) &
                      (is.na(bf$funding_funder_ids_crossref) |
                         !nzchar(bf$funding_funder_ids_crossref)))
n_answered1  <- sum(val$pilot == "pilot 1" & !is.na(val$mfund) & trimws(val$mfund) != "")

Of the 109 pilot-1 articles with a blank funding field, the pipeline finds funding for 90. Of those, 84 have a funding statement in the article’s own TEI and 57 carry a publisher-deposited Crossref funder ID — the publisher’s structured record of who paid for the work. Exactly 1 have neither. Only 52 pilot-1 articles carry an answer in the field.

Pilot 2 replaced the free-text box with a categorical question with forced options, so its blanks are genuinely unanswered rows and every answered row counts.

A known blind spot in conflict-of-interest capture

coi_category == "no statement" should be read with care for some publishers. Across both frames, 62.6% of articles carry a COI statement, but the rate by publisher runs from 13.4% for APA (10.1037, n = 1,036) to 95.7% for MDPI, with SAGE, Springer and Taylor & Francis all between 88% and 96%. That spread is too wide to be reporting culture alone.

Checking the source confirms it is a parsing limit. In the validation set, detection sensitivity is 92.9% outside APA and Cambridge but 50.0% within (n = 27). Taking one verified case, 10.1037/xap0000495: the PDF’s author note reads “The authors have no conflicts of interest to disclose”, and the 87,342-character GROBID TEI contains no match for conflict, competing interest, disclose or disclosure at all. APA places disclosures in the page-1 author note, and GROBID does not carry that note into the TEI. In a sample of 400 articles marked no statement, only 10.2% contain any COI wording in their TEI — so the absence is genuine for most, but not for the affected publishers.

Funding is not affected in the same way, because Crossref supplies structured funder IDs for 58.8% of APA articles and the pipeline uses them. There is no equivalent deposit for COI: a Crossref COI field exists for 7–9% of articles overall and rescued none.

Implication. For APA, Cambridge and 10.1192 — about 1,840 articles, 21% of the pooled dataset — no statement conflates “the article has none” with “we could not see it”, and treating it as an affirmative absence will produce a spurious publisher effect.

What is being done. This is metacheck issue #325. The maintainers expect it to be resolved by the forthcoming bibr import — bibr is the PDF-to-JSON extraction service replacing GROBID inside metacheck, and its author reports that it “has a section classification module that detects ethics/funding/coi sections very well”. We are seeking access to test that claim against this set, which is a good benchmark for it: 8,711 PDFs, 345 manually coded articles, publisher-level sensitivity measured, and 12 confirmed misses to check. bibr is not yet publicly released — there is no public repository, image or self-hosting documentation — so the test waits on either an API key or the server image. Until then the COI column stands as described, and the affected publishers should be handled explicitly in any analysis.

Every disagreement, article by article

The matrices above say how many cells disagree, not who was right. The table below lists every disagreeing article so that each one can be adjudicated against the source: what the pipeline said, what the coder said, the coder’s raw answer, and the evidence the pipeline acted on. Follow the DOI to check.

Code 
ev_trunc <- function(x, n = 160) {
  x <- gsub("\\s+", " ", x)
  ifelse(is.na(x) | !nzchar(x), "(nothing extracted)",
         ifelse(nchar(x) > n, paste0(substr(x, 1, n), "…"), x))
}

disagree <- bind_rows(
  val |> filter(!is.na(man_fund), funding_category != man_fund) |>
    transmute(Field = "funding_category", doi, Round = pilot,
              Pipeline = funding_category, Coder = man_fund,
              `Coder's raw answer` = ev_trunc(mfund),
              `Pipeline evidence` = ev_trunc(coalesce(funding_statement, funders))),
  val |> filter(!is.na(man_coi), coi_category != man_coi) |>
    transmute(Field = "coi_category", doi, Round = pilot,
              Pipeline = coi_category, Coder = man_coi,
              `Coder's raw answer` = ev_trunc(mcoi),
              `Pipeline evidence` = ev_trunc(coi_statement)),
  val |> filter(!is.na(man_prereg), prereg_present != man_prereg) |>
    transmute(Field = "prereg_present", doi, Round = pilot,
              Pipeline = as.character(prereg_present), Coder = as.character(man_prereg),
              `Coder's raw answer` = ev_trunc(mprereg),
              `Pipeline evidence` = ev_trunc(paste0(
                coalesce(prereg_platform, "no platform"), " — ",
                coalesce(prereg_url, "no URL"),
                ifelse(is_trial_registry, " [trial registry]", ""),
                ifelse(registration_any, " [registration_any = TRUE]", ""))))
) |> arrange(Field, Pipeline, Coder)

dis_tbl <- function(f) {
  disagree |>
    filter(Field == f) |>
    mutate(DOI = sprintf("[%s](https://doi.org/%s)", doi, doi)) |>
    select(DOI, Round, Pipeline, Coder, `Coder's raw answer`, `Pipeline evidence`) |>
    gt() |>
    fmt_markdown(columns = DOI) |>
    tab_header(title = paste(f, "— every disagreeing article"),
               subtitle = sprintf("%d of %d coded articles",
                                  sum(disagree$Field == f),
                                  sum(!is.na(val[[c(funding_category = "man_fund",
                                                    coi_category = "man_coi",
                                                    prereg_present = "man_prereg")[[f]]]])))) |>
    cols_width(DOI ~ px(230), Round ~ px(70), Pipeline ~ px(120), Coder ~ px(120),
               `Coder's raw answer` ~ px(240), `Pipeline evidence` ~ px(360)) |>
    tab_options(table.width = pct(100), table.font.size = px(13)) |>
    tab_style(style = cell_text(size = px(12)),
              locations = cells_body(columns = c(`Coder's raw answer`, `Pipeline evidence`))) |>
    tab_style(style = cell_text(whitespace = "nowrap"),
              locations = cells_body(columns = c(DOI, Round, Pipeline, Coder))) |>
    cols_align("left", columns = everything())
}

Download all 49 disagreements as CSV — for adjudicating offline and recording a verdict per row.

One pattern to check first. Several preregistration disagreements look definitional rather than factual: the pipeline separates a preregistration from a trial-registry entry, so an article registered on ClinicalTrials.gov gets prereg_present = FALSE but registration_any = TRUE, while a coder asked “were the studies preregistered?” may reasonably answer yes. Where the evidence column shows [trial registry], the two are answering different questions, and registration_any is the column that matches the coder’s intent.

Results

All figures below come from the two extraction outputs as they stand: 4,048 articles from the pilot-1 frame and 4,635 from the pilot-2 frame. Read differences between frames with care — the pilot-1 rows are restricted to articles classified empirical, the pilot-2 rows are not, and the two frames were drawn by different search strategies. The comparison the study is designed to make is within the pilot-2 frame, between keyword hits and non-hits.

Code 
share <- function(d, col) {
  d |> count(frame, value = .data[[col]]) |>
    group_by(frame) |> mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) |> ungroup()
}

fund_share   <- share(combined, "funding_category")
coi_share    <- share(combined, "coi_category")
reg_share    <- combined |>
  count(frame, value = registration_any) |>
  group_by(frame) |> mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) |> ungroup() |>
  mutate(value = ifelse(value, "registered", "not registered"))

pct <- function(d, v, f) {
  x <- d |> filter(frame == f, value == v)
  if (nrow(x) == 0) return("0%")
  sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x$pct)
}

Funding, conflicts of interest and registration

Code 
bind_rows(
  fund_share |> mutate(field = "Funding"),
  coi_share  |> mutate(field = "Conflict of interest"),
  reg_share  |> mutate(field = "Any registration")
) |>
  mutate(field = factor(field, c("Funding", "Conflict of interest", "Any registration"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(pct, value, fill = frame)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.65) +
  facet_wrap(~field, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PAL[1:2]) +
  labs(x = "Share of extracted articles", y = NULL, fill = NULL)
Code 
bind_rows(
  fund_share |> mutate(Field = "funding_category"),
  coi_share  |> mutate(Field = "coi_category"),
  reg_share  |> mutate(Field = "registration_any")
) |>
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", comma(n), 100 * pct)) |>
  select(Field, Category = value, frame, cell) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = frame, values_from = cell) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Field") |>
  tab_header(title = "Funding, COI and registration by frame") |>
  sub_missing(missing_text = "—") |>
  cols_align("left", columns = Category)

Three things stand out.

Funding statements are far more common in the pilot-1 frame — 81% of its articles are recorded as funded against 60% in the pilot-2 frame — and the gap runs the other way for articles with no funding statement at all. The frames’ journal mixes differ enough to explain this without any pipeline difference: the TOP Factor is missing for 1,717 pilot-2 articles against 255 in pilot 1, meaning the pilot-2 frame reaches further outside the set of journals with a recorded transparency policy.

Conflict-of-interest reporting goes the other way. A COI statement of some kind is present for 68.2% of pilot-2 articles against 56.2% of pilot-1 articles. Declared conflicts remain rare in both (8% and 6%); the common case by far is an explicit statement that there is no conflict.

Registration is a minority practice in both frames — 20% and 13% of articles report any registration at all.

Pilot-keyword screening

The pilot-2 index records whether the pilot-keyword screen (pilot, preliminary study, feasibility study) matched anywhere outside the reference list. This is the contrast the study is built around, and it only became available once the whole frame was converted: the PDFs converted first were themselves a keyword-selected subset, so the non-hit group did not exist as machine-readable text until now.

A keyword hit is a screen, not a coding decision — an article that mentions a pilot study someone else ran counts as a hit. Treat the contrast below as an upper bound on how cleanly the groups separate.

Code 
kw <- ex2 |>
  left_join(idx2 |> select(doi, keyword_hit), by = "doi") |>
  filter(!is.na(keyword_hit))

kw_test <- function(flag, label) {
  d <- kw |> mutate(y = flag)
  t <- table(d$keyword_hit, d$y)
  p <- prop.test(t[, "TRUE"], rowSums(t))
  tibble(
    Marker    = label,
    `No hit`  = p$estimate[[1]],
    `Hit`     = p$estimate[[2]],
    `Difference (pp)` = 100 * (p$estimate[[2]] - p$estimate[[1]]),
    `95% CI`  = sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", -100 * p$conf.int[2], -100 * p$conf.int[1]),
    p.value   = p$p.value)
}

kw_tbl <- bind_rows(
  kw_test(kw$funding_category == "funded",  "Funded"),
  kw_test(kw$coi_category != "no statement", "COI statement present"),
  kw_test(kw$prereg_present,                "Preregistration reported"),
  kw_test(kw$registration_any,              "Any registration"))
Code 
kw_tbl |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Pilot-keyword hits vs non-hits",
    subtitle = sprintf("%s hits, %s non-hits",
                       comma(sum(kw$keyword_hit)), comma(sum(!kw$keyword_hit)))) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = c(`No hit`, Hit), decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(columns = `Difference (pp)`, decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_scientific(columns = p.value, decimals = 1) |>
  cols_align("left", columns = Marker)

Articles the screen flags are markedly more likely to report a registration. Any registration rises from 11.0% among non-hits to 21.0% among hits — a difference of 10.1 pp (95% CI 6.9 to 13.3) — and preregistration specifically from 9.4% to 16.7%, 7.3 pp (95% CI 4.4 to 10.3). Funding follows the same direction more weakly, 7.7 pp (95% CI 3.8 to 11.6).

Conflict-of-interest reporting does not separate the groups: the difference is 3.1 pp (95% CI -0.6 to 6.8), an interval that includes zero.

Whether this reflects something about pilot studies or about the kind of research that mentions them is not something the screen can settle — it is a description of the frame, not a causal claim, and the manual coding is what will distinguish articles that report a pilot study from those that merely mention one.

Code 
kw_tbl |>
  select(Marker, `No hit`, Hit) |>
  pivot_longer(-Marker, names_to = "group", values_to = "p") |>
  mutate(Marker = factor(Marker, rev(kw_tbl$Marker))) |>
  ggplot(aes(p, Marker, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`No hit` = PAL[6], Hit = PAL[1])) +
  labs(x = "Share of articles", y = NULL, fill = "Keyword screen")

Reproducing this

# pilot-1 frame
Rscript run_full_sample.R

# pilot-2 frame
Rscript run_pilot2_sample.R

# validation against the manual coding
PIPELINE_RUN=1 Rscript run_pipeline.R

All three read from the on-disk caches under data/cache/, so a rerun makes no network calls. Column-by-column derivation rules are in docs/README_pipeline.md.
